wg.story.storm.text: Last night, a gentle storm blew through Wordroot Grove.

wg.story.open.text: By evening, every leaf in the Leaf Library had its label back.

wg.dlg.in.1.speaker: sarah

wg.help.prefix.text: Big words are made of smaller parts. Look at the beginning first.

wg.help.suffix.text: Big words are made of smaller parts. This time, check the ending.

wg.help.parts.text: Find the base word first, then its beginning and its ending.

wg.help.class.text: A word's job tells you its class. Endings give clues too.

wg.help.greek.text: Many science words grow from Greek roots. Each root has a meaning.

wg.hint.base.text: Don't skip the first part. It changes what the base word means.

wg.hint.build.text: Check each part's meaning. Does it match the meaning you need?

wg.hint.sort.noun.text: Endings like -ness and -ment often make a noun. Does it name a thing?

wg.hint.sort.verb.text: The ending -en often makes a verb. Is it something you can do?
wg.hint.sort.verb.speaker: gloop

wg.hint.sort.adjective.text: Endings like -ful, -less and -able often make an adjective. Does it describe?
wg.hint.sort.adjective.speaker: gloop

wg.hint.sort.adverb.text: The ending -ly often makes an adverb. Does it tell how?
wg.hint.sort.adverb.speaker: gloop

wg.hint.sort.trap.text: Careful: not every -ly word is an adverb. In a costly gift, costly describes.

wg.hint.fit.adjective.text: The gap describes something. Which word describes?

wg.hint.clue.definition.text: Words right after a comma, or after is, often explain the mystery word.

wg.hint.clue.synonym.text: Or can give another name for the mystery word.
wg.hint.clue.synonym.speaker: gloop

wg.hint.clue.example.text: Such as and like give examples. What do the examples have in common?
wg.hint.clue.example.speaker: gloop

wg.hint.clue.restatement.text: In other words, that is, and which means say it again more simply.
wg.hint.clue.restatement.speaker: gloop

wg.hint.clue.cause.text: Because and so link what happened to why. What would cause that?
wg.hint.clue.cause.speaker: gloop

wg.hint.clue.contrast.text: But, unlike, although, however and while signal an opposite.
wg.hint.clue.contrast.speaker: gloop

wg.hint.clue.multi.text: The other sentences show what the word is like. What do they point to?
wg.hint.clue.multi.speaker: gloop

wg.hint.owners.text: Count the owners. One owner, or more than one?
wg.hint.owners.speaker: gloop

wg.hint.own.text: The things belong to someone. That needs an apostrophe.
wg.hint.own.speaker: gloop

wg.hint.its.text: Try it is in the gap. If it works, use it's. If not, its.
wg.hint.its.speaker: gloop

wg.hint.plural.text: Does anything belong to them, or is it just more than one?
wg.hint.plural.speaker: gloop

wg.hint.irregular.text: This plural has no s at the end. Add apostrophe s to show the owners.
wg.hint.irregular.speaker: gloop

wg.hint.contraction.text: Which letters are missing? The apostrophe goes in their place.
wg.hint.contraction.speaker: gloop

wg.hint.they.text: Try they are in the gap. Does it still make sense?
wg.hint.they.speaker: gloop

wg.hint.to.text: Is it a number? Does it mean also, or too much? Or does it point somewhere?
wg.hint.to.speaker: gloop

wg.hint.you.text: Try you are in the gap. Does it still make sense?
wg.hint.you.speaker: gloop

wg.hint.than.text: Are you comparing two things, or telling what came next?
wg.hint.than.speaker: gloop

wg.hint.test.text: Try each word in the sentence and read it again.
wg.hint.test.speaker: gloop

wg.hint.show.text: Let's work it out together, step by step.
wg.hint.show.speaker: sarah

wg.hint.model.text: Now you finish it. The answer is glowing.
wg.hint.model.speaker: sarah

wg.retry.1.text: Not yet. Let's look at the parts.

wg.p.plimbet.text: Ana packed a plimbet, a small bag for carrying a snack, before the hike.

wg.p.drinnet.text: Kofi filled his drinnet, or water bottle, at the fountain.

wg.p.sorbinet.text: Mei wore a sorbinet, a warm hat with flaps over the ears, in the snow.

wg.p.quosset.text: Raj keeps every quosset, such as apples, pears and plums, in a blue bowl.

wg.p.morrick.text: The trail was morrick; in other words, it was steep and hard to climb, so Lena rested often.

wg.p.klendor.text: Omar fed the klendor, a tiny fish with orange stripes, that lives in his tank.

wg.p.bramtock.text: Zara swept the bramtock, or front porch, after the storm.

wg.p.brindop.text: Tomás hung each brindop, like his hammer and his saw, on the workshop wall.

wg.p.gendrop.text: Priya used a gendrop, which is a long spoon for stirring soup, to mix dinner.

wg.p.pentrop.text: A pentrop is a party held outside in a park, and Jonah loves them.

wg.p.galdrup.text: Nia found a galdrup, or smooth, flat stone, by the river.

wg.p.holtip.text: Sami's favorite holtip, such as soccer or swimming, keeps him busy all week.

wg.p.torvish.text: The puppy felt torvish, which means very sleepy, after its long walk.

wg.p.lomvish.text: Kenji's soup was lomvish, or warm but not hot, so he ate it right away.

wg.p.valdish.text: The room was valdish, that is, very neat and tidy, after Aiyana cleaned it.

wg.p.crennish.text: The bread smelled crennish, fresh and warm from the oven, when Ana opened the door.

wg.p.skelvy.text: Raj loves skelvy weather, like windy days with gray clouds, for flying kites.

wg.p.trevvy.text: Lena felt trevvy, or nervous, before her piano recital.

wg.p.prendle.text: Zara will prendle the plants, which means give them a little water, every morning.

wg.p.ravvle.text: Kofi likes to ravvle, or hum quietly, while he draws.

wg.p.wezzle.text: Mei's cat will wezzle, in other words, curl up in a ball, on any warm blanket.

wg.p.sprock.text: Omar had to sprock the tent, or fold it up small, before the drive home.

wg.p.splott.text: The baby likes to splott, which means clap and stamp at the same time, when music plays.

wg.p.grimvel.text: Before the race, Nia grimveled, or stretched her legs, on the grass.

wg.p.flimmet.text: The cave was flimmet. Omar couldn't see his own hand. He switched on his flashlight. His friends waited outside.

wg.p.blistom.text: Kenji's brother is blistom, but Kenji is quiet. His brother shouts and sings all day long. They both like pizza.

wg.p.snorbit.text: Because the path was snorbit, Ana slipped twice. She stepped slowly over the icy stones. Her friends waited by the gate.

wg.p.fendro.text: Raj's lunch was fendro. He took one bite and fanned his mouth. Then he gulped down a whole glass of water. The cafeteria was busy that day.

wg.p.grevin.text: Although the puppy looked grevin, it was full of energy. It had just run, jumped and chased its tail for an hour. Sami named it Biscuit.

wg.p.skorvel.text: The lemonade was so skorvel that Zara added three spoons of sugar. Even then, her lips puckered. She sat under a big tree.

wg.p.kerpin.text: Nia carried the kerpin to the lake. She climbed in and picked up the paddle. Soon she was gliding across the water. Ducks swam nearby.

wg.p.lumbrit.text: Instead of walking, Jonah decided to lumbrit. He raced down the hill as fast as he could. He reached the bottom first. His shoes were blue.

wg.p.zorvel.text: The thunder was zorvel. Aiyana covered her ears. The windows rattled in their frames. Then the rain began.

wg.p.quandrel.text: Priya practices her quandrel every evening. She plucks its four strings, and soft music fills the room. Her room is painted green.

wg.p.fennick.text: Most of the class felt fennick before the test, but Lena felt calm. Their hands shook as they waited for the papers.

wg.p.flaxim.text: Omar needed a flaxim to cross the stream. He laid the long wooden board over the water. Then he walked across it carefully. A frog watched him.

wg.p.nubbick.text: The kitten was nubbick, so it hid under the bed. It shook whenever the doorbell rang. Its fur was gray.

wg.p.tumvick.text: Kofi thought the movie would be tumvick, but it was exciting from start to finish. He had expected to yawn the whole time. He shared popcorn with Mei.

wg.p.ulbrin.text: Grandpa keeps an ulbrin by the door. When it rains, he opens it and holds it over his head. He always wears a red coat.

wg.p.mirvane.text: The old bridge was mirvane, so the town closed it. Its boards were cracked and loose. A new bridge will open in May.

wg.p.glantrip.text: Tomás wanted a glantrip after his long swim. He stretched out on a soft towel and closed his eyes for an hour. The pool was busy.

wg.p.kopwell.text: Unlike the kopwell old road, the new road is smooth. The old road is full of bumps and holes. Buses use both roads.

wg.p.crosvin.text: Zara's shoes were crosvin after she jumped in every puddle. Water squished out with each step. She laughed all the way home.

wg.p.nalvick.text: Sami pinned the nalvick to the wall. It showed every town on the island and every road between them. He used a red pin.

wg.p.tolvane.text: Ana's old backpack was tolvane. However, her new one is light and easy to carry. The old one hurt her shoulders. Both are purple.

wg.p.umbrick.text: The soup was umbrick, so Kenji blew on each spoonful. Steam rose from the bowl. He ate it with bread.

wg.p.wistrop.text: Mei used a wistrop to dig in the garden. Its sharp metal end cut through the soil, and its long handle saved her back. The tulips bloomed in spring.

wg.p.crandiv.text: While Raj's dog is crandiv, his cat is lazy. The dog runs, fetches and plays all afternoon. Both pets sleep at night.
